stories.title: P0: bake the BT rfkill-unblock fix into deploy (make the live capture fix repo-managed + reflash-proof)
acceptance: add deploy/eclipse-rfkill-unblock.service: oneshot `rfkill unblock all`, After=systemd-rfkill.service bluetooth.service, WantedBy=multi-user.target (exactly the unit Atlas installed live tonight)
add a deploy-pi.sh step that installs + enables the unit (sync-if-changed, idempotent) AND clears any stale /var/lib/systemd/rfkill/*:bluetooth block state on deploy
full implementation spec (exact unit + step + acceptance) is in Ralph's inbox: offices/ralph/inbox/2026-07-31-from-atlas-bake-rfkill-unblock-into-deploy.md -- build to it
does NOT use deploy --init (a normal deploy makes it repo-managed; --init is the exact path that would have wiped the live fix)
tests cover the deploy-pi.sh step (unit installed + enabled + stale-block cleared); ruff clean

validationCriteria.action: after PM deploys this + reboots the Pi (bench, no car)
validationCriteria.outcome: `rfkill list` shows BOTH hci0:Bluetooth and phy0:Wireless LAN Soft blocked:no; `systemctl is-enabled eclipse-rfkill-unblock`=enabled; eclipse-obd active

stories.goal: As the deploy path, I want the eclipse-rfkill-unblock fix in the repo + deploy-pi.sh, so the capture fix (currently live-on-Pi-by-hand) survives a reflash / deploy --init and can't silently revert to the soft-block that killed capture since 07-03.

stories.title: P0: fix scripts/pair_obdlink.sh (Trixie bluez prompt regex + display-capable agent) so a durable bond + trust is written
acceptance: fix the pexpect prompt regex: it expects `\[.+\]#` but Trixie bluetoothctl prompts `[bluetoothctl]>` -> it times out and never pairs. Match the real prompt

change the agent from `NoInputNoOutput` (contradicts the script's own Confirm-passkey handling -> auth-fails on the OBDLink) to a display-capable agent (`DisplayYesNo`) so a durable bond + `trust` is written and survives reboot
full implementation spec (file:line for both bugs + acceptance) is in Ralph's inbox: offices/ralph/inbox/2026-07-31-from-atlas-fix-pair-obdlink-sh.md -- build to it
--dry-run still MUST NOT invoke bluetoothctl or any external BT stack (preserve the existing guard); tests cover the regex match + agent selection; ruff clean

validationCriteria.action: run the fixed script's dry-run + unit tests (code/logic layer, bench)
validationCriteria.outcome: the prompt regex matches `[bluetoothctl]>` + the agent is display-capable; dry-run stays inert. NOTE: full pair + bond-survives-reboot verification is engine-on -- Spool owns that live gate

conditionalOutcomes: the code fix is bench/unit-testable now; the real pair + bond-survives-reboot is engine-on (Spool) and folds into the BL-025 validation drive
stories.goal: As the pairing tool, I want pair_obdlink.sh to actually pair + trust + bond the OBDLink on Trixie bluez, so a durable bond survives reboot and re-pairing works instead of timing out.
